chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: Ubayd ibn Kharija narrated to us, from Ali ibn Uthman, from Furat ibn Ahnaf, from Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his fathers, saying:

The Euphrates overflowed during the time of the Commander of the Faithful, so he rode out with his two sons, al-Hasan and al-Husayn. They passed by the tribe of Thaqif, who said: 'Ali has come to drive back the water.' Imam Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, I and these two sons of mine will be killed, and Allah will send a man from my descendants at the end of time who will claim our blood, and he will be in occultation from them, as a distinction for the people of deviation, until the ignorant will say: Allah has no need of the family of Muhammad.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali (as) predict about the occultation of the Mahdi and the reaction of the ignorant?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the prophetic foresight of Imam Ali (AS) regarding the Mahdi, linking the immediate political struggle with the eschatological destiny of the Ahl al-Bayt. The mention of 'the ignorant' (*al-jahil*) questioning the utility of the Prophet's progeny reflects the Shia theological concept of the Great Occultation (*al-Ghaybah al-Kubra*), where the Imam's absence serves as a divine test to distinguish true believers from those who abandon the lineage due to lack of knowledge.
